title: Count the shoots
scenario: A vine grows a new shoot each month — as many as the last two months put together. Month 1: 1 shoot, month 2: 1 shoot. How many shoots in month 6?

intro.job: A vine grows a new shoot each month — as many as the last two months put together. Month 1: 1 shoot, month 2: 1 shoot. How many shoots in month 6?

idea.rule: Both branches count — fib(n) is fib(n-1) plus fib(n-2), not just one of them.
idea.detail: Each month's count is the two months before it added together: 1, 1, 2, 3, 5, 8. So fib(n) calls itself TWICE — once for last month, once for the month before — and adds the two answers. The base case (months 1 and 2 are 1) stops the calls; both branches have to come back and be added, or the count never grows.

model_restatement: Work out month n's count, where each month is the sum of the two months before it.

clarify.question: Where does the count start?
clarify.answer: Month 1 and month 2 both have 1 shoot.

clarify.question: Does it need to be fast for big months?
clarify.answer: Not today — n is small. Speed is the alternative's story.

clarify_fallback: Good question — assume the simple case.
blueprint: fib(n) is built from the month before. Months 1 and 2 are 1. Print fib(n).

checkpoints.prompt: When the base case first runs (line 3), what is n?
On the print line, what is answer?

why_line: return fib(n - 1) follows one branch all the way down to month 2 and hands back its 1 — nothing is ever added, so every month comes out as 1.

explain.rule: Counting only one branch is asking just one parent how many grandchildren there are — you get one family tree's worth, and the other half of the vine is never counted.
explain.bridge: Month 6 is month 5 plus which other month?

fix.rule: fib(n - 1) + fib(n - 2): both earlier months come back, and their counts are added.

walk.gloss: Any later month: last month plus the month before, both counted.
Start the chain at month n.

alternatives.note: Remember each month's count so you never count it twice — correct, and the fast way once the numbers get big.
